decisions.statement: The package built is the package a container's working directory names.
A workload no container syncs code into has no build made for that workload.
A plan naming no workload names nothing for a pod to build.
The sha built is the sha the caller names.
Whether origin has a sha is asked of origin rather than of a local ref.
Nothing here puts a commit onto origin.
Whether a tree installs is asked of the manifests that tree tracks rather than of the worktree.
Only the manifests a tree tracks and the lockfile beside those manifests are taken out of the tree.
An install proved this way writes nothing into the tree the install was proved from.
A workspace a tree names and tracks no manifest for is named in the refusal.
The scratch an install is proved in is swept whether the proof passed or failed.
No whole tree is laid out to prove an install.
The pod is checked out to the sha before the build runs.
A checkout failing for a reason that passes is tried again.
The workload is restarted onto the build and waited on until its rollout is done.
A build restarts the workload only where no apply is about to roll that workload.
A build run leaves the sha that run was made from inside the build that run made.
The builder is run from the checkout rather than through a script in the folder built.
A build is written into a scratch beside the folder the pod serves.
The folder the pod serves is replaced only once a build is made whole.
A build that fails leaves the folder the pod serves as that folder was.
The scratch a build failed in is swept before the next build begins.
The values a build needs are the values the manifest code exports beside the manifests.
A value a build needs that a cluster secret has is read from that secret.
A value a build needs that nothing has stops the build before the build starts.
The sha built is among the values the build is handed.
No value read from a secret is carried into the text reported.
A refusal reports the last lines said with every stack frame dropped.
A failure saying nothing but stack frames is reported by those frames.
Whether a build already exists is asked of the pod holding the build.
A pod already going away has no build.
Nothing here reads a page.
Nothing here applies a manifest.
Every web app's build sits in a host path on the one node that serves that web app.
A build is made somewhere other than the pod that serves that build.

definition: the build a web app's pod serves, made in that pod from what a workstation holds
